target_customer: Large cattle ranches and graziers in Australia, expanding to US ranchers
problem: Mustering cattle takes helicopters, motorbikes, horses and a full crew for a day. The company claims drones can do it on a schedule at roughly half the cost.
business_model: Pilot rollout with waitlist and free on-site demo; pricing not published
product_category: Autonomous drones and AI for livestock mustering and pasture monitoring

founders.name: Sam Rogers
education: University of Sydney, dropped out of robotics
founders.background_notes: YC page bio says he spent half his life on a cattle farm and half building robots. Launch post says his family runs a cattle station. Only founder listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs reinforcement learning models that respond to animal behavior, autonomous drone flight, offline operation near a base station, and computer vision for counting and pasture analysis, all built by a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary herding models trained on live mustering data and relationships with large ranches. Competitors exist in Australia and drone hardware is commodity, so the moat rests on the models.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found. Small Australian rivals (SkyKelpie, Drone-Hand) pursued similar ideas at the same time.

market_need_then: Large Australian stations spend heavily on helicopters and labor for mustering, and labor is scarce. Pilot farms covering about 700,000 hectares were reported lined up in Queensland and NSW in early 2026.

branding.domain_note: brumby.com, the exact name; the company site announced the rename from GrazeMate in July 2026

identity.voice_and_tone: Practical and plain, aimed at farm operators; taglines 'Precision grazing, on autopilot' and 'Your property, in your pocket'

branding.brand_signature: Robot cowboys that herd cattle with drones

rebrands.why: Not stated; the site says same product, team and mission

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of the teenage founder in Forbes Australia, Startup Daily and AgFunder News; no merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Brumby is the Australian word for a wild horse, which fits the cowboy imagery and is memorable. Press leaned on the 'robot cowboys' story, though the new name is months old.

outcome_analysis: Active and early. The founder grew up on a cattle station, which gives unusual domain insight and access to pilot ranches. A 19 year old founder raising a YC led pre-seed with pilots across Queensland and NSW is a strong start, but revenue is not public and pricing is unpublished. Hardware, regulation of drone flight and US expansion are the main risks.
notes: Round reported as $1.2 million (Forbes Australia headline, Startup Daily, Dealroom) announced 2026-02-02; currency is unclear (Dealroom says A$, Startup Daily does not state it), so amount_usd is null. Meat & Livestock Australia appears as an investor in one search summary only and is left out. Competitor source dates were not visible in the pages seen, so source_date is null. No shutdown, acquisition or layoff news found. Competitors SkyKelpie (Queensland paddock trials with MLA, work possibly dating to 2022), Drone-Hand (launched 2023) and Sphere Drones (Wagga Wagga trials) were found only in undated or later coverage, so the dated list is left empty.
